title: Zapline SDK: First 7 Days Bootcamp Script
body:
Goal
A compact, repeatable 7-day bootcamp script for new internal integrators and selected customers to go from zero to an instrumented sample integration using the Zapline SDK (JS + Python patterns). Focus: fast wins, observable reliability, and prompt/eval gating so teams can prove low risk by Day 7.

Audience
- New engineer or PM starting integration with Redwood SDKs
- Solutions engineers running onboarding sessions
- Partner engineers evaluating embedded flows

Constraints / assumptions
- Attendee has basic dev environment (Node 16+/Python 3.10+, Git)
- We provide a repo with three tiny sample apps: chat-proto, bulk-embed, rerank-demo
- 2 hours/day allocation is realistic for busy teams; optionally condensed to 1 full day workshop

High-level week plan (intent + deliverable per day)
Day 0 (prep, asynchronous): repo clone + creds
  - Deliverable: forked repo, API key configured in .env, can run smoke command `npm run smoke` or `python -m zapline.smoke`
  - Quick checklist: node, python, git, docker (optional), network allowlist note

Day 1: Hello request & local dev loop (first 30 minutes success)
  - Walkthrough: minimal chat request using SDK client (JS and Python snippets)
  - Deliverable: sample app returns a single generated message and logs a trace id
  - Teaching points: auth, timeouts, streaming toggle, ephemeral vs persistent keys
  - Troubleshooting notes: common 401, CORS for browser example (proxy guidance)

Day 2: Observability + Telemetry basics
  - Instrument calls: add SDK telemetry hooks (event names below), wire to Console dev dashboard
  - Deliverable: invocation-level latency histogram, token-cost log, one tagged error event in dev account
  - Telemetry events (recommended naming): `zapline.request.start`, `zapline.request.end`, `zapline.stream.chunk`, `zapline.kvcache.hit`, `zapline.request.error`, `zapline.eval.testcase.result`
  - Gating: set alert threshold for p95 latency > 700ms on small model in dev

Day 3: Prompt harness + deterministic smoke tests
  - Add a small prompt suite (3 canonical prompts) and expected-bucket checks (contains key phrase / length range)
  - Deliverable: CI job that runs prompt suite and fails on obvious regressions
  - Quick CI snippet: GitHub Actions job that runs `pytest tests/prompt_suite.py` and uploads minimal telemetry artifact

Day 4: Cost controls and batching patterns
  - Teach: continuous batching, batch size heuristics, cache-first prefixes, token cap per request
  - Deliverable: toggles in config to switch between `latency-first` and `cost-first` profiles; run load sim (local loop) to show cost delta
  - Example heuristic: batch if concurrency > 6 or token-window > 512; else passthrough

Day 5: Rollout + fallback flows
  - Demo: canary traffic flow across two model variants; automatic fallback to smaller quantized variant
  - Deliverable: feature-flagged route + sample test that flips flag and validates fallback behavior
  - Rollback triggers: error ratio spike > 2% for 10m OR quality regression (prompt suite failure) > 10%

Day 6: Private deployment checklist (light)
  - Cover: KMS integration pointers, VPC egress allowlist, local artifact packaging
  - Deliverable: runbook section that lists required infra items and a smoke checklist to hand to ops
  - Note: for air-gapped customers include steps to sign the model artifacts and provide SHA checksums

Day 7: Customer-facing demo + handoff artifacts
  - Deliverable: 10-min demo script, PR to include `docs/first-7-days.md` in the repo, and a short retro note capturing remaining risks
  - Handoff bundle: .env.example, minimal Grafana dashboard panel JSON, prompt-suite.csv, CI job yaml, runbook.md

Session templates (30–90 minute blocks)
- 30-min coaching: 10m setup + 15m guided pair-program + 5m next steps
- 60-min workshop: 15m overview + 35m paired lab + 10m Q&A and action items
- 90-min deep-dive: 20m architecture + 50m hands-on + 20m telemetry & rollout planning

Micro-labs (copyable instructions for repo)
- Lab A (15m): Add request-level tracing id to all SDK calls and emit it in console logs
- Lab B (20m): Create a telemetry event that increments when a KV-cache hit occurs and check it appears in dev dashboard
- Lab C (30m): Implement a tiny prompt-suite test and wire to a GitHub action that blocks merges on failure

Recommended repo layout (minimal)
- /samples/chat-proto/
- /samples/bulk-embed/
- /samples/rerank-demo/
- /tests/prompt-suite.csv
- /ci/actions/prompt-suite.yml
- /docs/first-7-days.md (auto-generated from this script)
- /ops/runbook-md (deployment checklist)

Acceptance criteria by Day 7 (engineering + product)
- Roundtrip success: sample app returns expected output for 3 canonical prompts
- Observability: latency and cost metrics visible in Console and wired to alerting
- Quality gate: prompt-suite passes in CI on main branch
- Safety: private deployment checklist reviewed with security (if applicable)

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self)
- Decide whether to include a browser-based quickstart (CORS / proxy guidance) or keep only server-side examples
- Add a tiny serverless example (Vercel/AWS Lambda) – need guidance on cold-starts and token cache
- Flesh out example token-budget calculator (spreadsheet) for customers doing cost projections
- Confirm telemetry sampling default (currently thinking 10% for hosted dev accounts)

Failure modes & recovery playbook (short)
- 401s: check key rotation and environment variable precedence; provide `zapline whoami` CLI debug
- High latency: switch to `latency-first` profile, reduce batch window, increase fallback ratio
- Prompt regression: revert to previous pinned model; if pinned model unavailable, fallback to canonical small-model route

Script author notes (meta)
- Use this as a stand-alone workshop guide for SEs and as the basis for `docs/first-7-days.md` to ship in repo
- Keep labs intentionally small — each day must produce an observable artifact
- Encourage teams to schedule a Day 8 follow-up to convert lab artifacts into production runbooks

Quick links for facilitators
- SDK repo PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/zapline-sdk/pull/128
- Sample demo playground: https://console.redwood.ai/dev/playground/zapline-samples
- Telemetry schema draft (internal): CONFLUENCE-DEVEXP-207

Revision history
- 2024-04-30 Maya Chen: initial draft and skeleton
- 2024-05-14 Liam Walker: telemetry event names and acceptance criteria additions

Notes: this is a working doc. Keep it light, add bits to the repo as small, reviewable PRs.
